source: Hand-authored by Evidentia. Maps the eight FDA Section 524B premarket security control categories to coarse, high-level ANSI/AAMI SW96:2023 security-risk-management process areas. SW96 internal section numbers are NOT asserted (the standard is paywalled and was not inspected from a primary source); the target IDs are Evidentia's own coarse process-area labels.
verification_note: These mappings are ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual links authored by Evidentia, not independently audited and not endorsed by the FDA or ANSI/AAMI. The target side maps to coarse, high-level SW96 process areas (no internal clause/section numbers are asserted). They are intended to orient a reader between the 524B security control categories and the SW96 security-risk-management process; they are not a control-equivalence assertion. Consumers MUST verify any reliance against the licensed ANSI/AAMI SW96:2023 text and the FDA guidance.
risk_model_note: Safety risk management (ISO 14971:2019) characterizes risk as a combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm (commonly operationalized as probability × severity). Security risk management (ANSI/AAMI SW96:2023, building on AAMI TIR57:2016 (R2023)) characterizes security risk in terms of exploitability rather than probability of occurrence, while sharing the same patient-harm severity axis — a security exploit is assessed by how readily it can be carried out (exploitability) combined with the severity of the resulting patient harm. The FDA Section 524B premarket security controls feed the device's security risk management, which in turn informs the ISO 14971 safety risk file via the shared severity axis. This characterization is a paraphrase of the ISO 14971 and AAMI SW96/TIR57 methodologies, not a quotation from the FDA guidance or the standards.
